entry.title: IT Consultant - Microsoft Access
entry.content:
As an independent IT consultant, I worked with a local organization to evaluate and improve usability within a legacy Microsoft Access application. My focus was on streamlining workflows, reducing manual effort, and enhancing clarity within an existing system without disrupting operational continuity. A primary objective was enabling the owner to easily generate meaningful reports to better understand and manage business processes.

Responsibilities

  • Evaluated and improved user workflows within a legacy Microsoft Access application.
  • Identified usability challenges and implemented interface and logic improvements using VBA.
  • Collaborated with business stakeholders to understand user needs and translate them into system enhancements.
  • Performed testing and validation to ensure changes were reliable and did not disrupt existing workflows.

Problem

The organization relied on a legacy Microsoft Access application to manage internal workflows. Over time, the system became difficult to navigate and maintain due to:

  • Inconsistent form behavior

  • Manual processes that increased user effort

  • Limited feedback for user actions

  • Growing complexity in logic and reporting

Users needed a more streamlined, intuitive workflow without requiring a complete system overhaul.

Process & Impact

I began by analyzing the database structure, form layouts, and existing VBA logic to understand how users interacted with the system and where friction occurred. I also collaborated closely with the stakeholder to document requested changes and prioritize enhancements based on workflow impact.

  • Mapped user workflows to identify bottlenecks and redundant manual steps

  • Identified usability challenges in form design and interaction feedback

  • Implemented VBA enhancements to automate repetitive tasks

  • Simplified form logic to create clearer, more predictable interactions

  • Collaborated directly with stakeholders to translate operational needs into practical improvements

  • Tested and validated changes to ensure reliability and minimize disruption

Reflection

Working within a legacy system reinforced the importance of balancing user needs with technical constraints. I learned that meaningful UX improvements often come from careful workflow evaluation and incremental enhancements rather than rebuilding from scratch. This experience strengthened my ability to analyze user behavior, simplify complex processes, and deliver practical solutions within real-world limitations.

entry.title: Case In Point - Noble Community Clinics
entry.content:
As part of UW–Stevens Point’s Case In Point business competition, my team developed a UX-focused strategy to help Noble Community Clinics attract and retain dental professionals in rural communities. We applied user research, competitive analysis, usability testing, and wireframing to redesign Noble’s careers experience. Our solution earned first place in the competition.

You can view our mockup here!

Noble Community Clinics - Career Page Mockup
Case In Point Article

Problem

Noble Community Clinics faced challenges attracting dental professionals to rural areas. Through initial stakeholder meetings, we identified that:

  • The careers page lacked strong employee-focused messaging

  • The website emphasized patient information over employee experience

  • The brand did not clearly communicate workplace culture

  • Rural relocation concerns (community, family, belonging) were not addressed

  • The goal was to redesign the careers experience to make potential employees feel welcomed and connected before they even relocated.

Process & Impact

Research & Stakeholder Interviews

  • Met with the Noble leadership team to gather goals and challenges

  • Identified key priorities: culture, mission, employee relationships, social media presence

  • Shifted perspective from a client-focused site to a people-focused recruitment strategy

Competitive Analysis

  • Evaluated competitor career pages

  • Identified strengths such as community storytelling, culture highlights, and clear calls to action

  • Noted gaps in Noble’s presentation compared to certified employers

Usability Testing

Conducted usability testing with participants across multiple age groups and professional backgrounds:

  • 25-year-old shift lead

  • 60-year-old IT systems administrator

  • 20-year-old college student

Key findings:

  • Users were unsure what type of clinic Noble was

  • The work environment felt unclear

  • Career growth information was limited

  • The page felt informational but not inviting

Wireframing & Design (Adobe XD)

  • Developed a redesigned careers page mockup

  • Prioritized culture, growth, and community integration

  • Simplified layout and clarified information hierarchy

  • Highlighted social media presence and employee experience

  • Integrated community partnerships and relocation support information

Results

  • Delivered a complete UX redesign proposal

  • Presented strategic implementation plan

  • Proposed social media and certification strategy to improve employer branding

  • Earned first place in the Case In Point competition

Reflection

This experience strengthened my ability to approach UX from both a user and strategic perspective. I learned how recruitment experiences differ from traditional consumer-facing UX and how storytelling, community integration, and clear messaging influence decision-making. Collaborating in a multidisciplinary team environment reinforced the importance of research, iteration, and alignment with stakeholder goals.

entry.title: BizSquad - Seeds of Hope
entry.content:
As part of BizSquad, a multidisciplinary consulting team at Fox Valley Technical College, I contributed to a UX and engagement strategy for Seeds of Hope, a financial assistance fund supporting students. The goal was to improve awareness, clarify the application process, and increase engagement across students, donors, and referrals.

Seeds of Hope Main Page

Responsibilities

  • Designed new web pages and enhanced existing ones using Adobe Illustrator, improving organization's visual identity and user experience.

  • Developed a strategic content outline to expand the organization's outreach efforts, increasing engagement with key audiences.

  • Partnered with organization leaders to ensure website redesign aligned with their goals, resulting in a more effective communication platform.

Problem

Seeds of Hope faced challenges engaging students, donors, and referral sources. Through stakeholder discussions and engagement analysis, we identified:

  • Limited awareness of the organization’s mission

  • Confusion around the application process

  • Inconsistent visibility across engagement channels

  • Lack of storytelling to connect emotionally with potential donors

  • The objective was to improve clarity, strengthen messaging, and design a more engaging digital presence.

Process & Impact

Engagement Channel Analysis

  • Mapped how students, donors, and referrals discovered Seeds of Hope

  • Identified gaps between awareness and action

  • Created engagement charts to visualize touchpoints

Information Architecture & Content Strategy

  • Developed a website blueprint to clarify content structure

  • Proposed a new storytelling-focused page to highlight the organization’s impact

  • Simplified the application explanation to reduce confusion

  • Outlined roadmap for improving engagement across channels

Implementation Support

  • Submitted change requests to improve clarity on the existing page

  • Designed a new page concept focused on mission and story

  • Collaborated with leadership and marketing stakeholders to align UX improvements with organizational goals

Results

  • Delivered a formal engagement and UX strategy report

  • Created roadmap prioritizing high-impact improvements

  • Improved clarity of application process

  • Strengthened alignment between mission messaging and digital experience

  • Contributed approximately 55 hours of project management and 50 hours of web design and analysis

BizSquad - Fall 2024 Report Out

Reflection

This project reinforced how UX extends beyond interface design into engagement strategy and content architecture. I learned the importance of mapping user journeys across multiple channels and balancing stakeholder goals with user clarity. Working within time and platform constraints strengthened my ability to prioritize high-impact improvements and communicate strategic recommendations effectively.

entry.title: BizSquad - Fox Valley Trout Unlimited
entry.content:
A UX-focused volunteer project to improve the usability, navigation, and accessibility of the Fox Valley Trout Unlimited website. The goal was to help visitors quickly find key information such as events, membership details, and conservation initiatives on both desktop and mobile devices.

Fox Valley Trout Unlimited is an active chapter of Trout Unlimited located in the Fox Valley southwest of Green Bay Wisconsin.

Trout Unlimited's Main Page

Responsibilities

  • Developed a strategic approach to enhance the organization’s online presence, which improved engagement with members and increased visibility within the community.
  • Reorganized and restructured WordPress website to better align with organization’s goals, enhancing site navigation, user experience, and ensuring mobile responsiveness for better accessibility on all devices.
  • Produced engaging video content to effectively communicate organization's mission and events.
  • Integrated Facebook feed into website to streamline event promotion, leading to more efficient event management and improved participation from members.
  • Worked closely with organization leaders ensuring digital strategies were in line with their vision, creating a more unified and effective online presence.

Problem

Users struggled to find priority content due to inconsistent layout, overwhelming navigation choices, and unclear content hierarchy. This created confusion around tasks like finding upcoming events, joining the organization, or learning about local initiatives.

Process

  • Evaluated existing site structure to understand common navigation paths

  • Conducted informal stakeholder interviews to define user priorities

  • Mapped user task flows to identify friction points

  • Conducted informal usability testing by walking through common user tasks and gathering stakeholder feedback to identify navigation friction, unclear content hierarchy, and areas of cognitive overload.

  • Simplified navigation by reducing clutter and prioritizing commonly accessed sections

  • Reorganized content hierarchy to highlight events and membership information

  • Tested layout responsiveness across mobile and tablet devices

Design Decisions

  • Consolidated navigation items into clearer, task-centered categories

  • Emphasized key calls to action such as “Upcoming Events” and “Get Involved”

  • Improved spacing and typography for better scanability

  • Adjusted layouts for consistent behavior between desktop and mobile views

  • Applied accessibility-aware design practices such as clear headings and consistent labels

Impact

  • Navigation became easier to follow, reducing cognitive load

  • Key content (events, membership) became more prominent and easier to access

  • Site visuals and layout felt more consistent and cohesive

  • Stakeholders reported improved clarity and reduced visitor confusion

  • Mobile usability increased through responsive adjustments

Reflection

This project reinforced the value of user-centered design and thoughtful information architecture. I learned how subtle adjustments to layout and navigation can significantly improve usability—especially for diverse audiences accessing the site on multiple devices.
